summary: TEN MEASURED CHECKS, all PASS, every one reading the finished solids (../../../../out/mech/verdicts.json): envelope 31.874 x 31.874 x 7.980 mm against SPEC section 4; the maximum diameter occurs where Apple's drawing puts it; all five of section 4's stepped diameters are present on a solid; the annulus Ø31.874..Ø37.31 contains no halo material, so the antenna keep-out is entirely the host's obligation; the seven conductive parts are named with their diameters rather than hidden; the bayonet passes five probes INCLUDING the two that must be non-zero; the pressed door has 0.0000 mm3 of travel obstruction; the bender clears the board by 1.080 mm and the carrier by 1.912 mm; the door seal squeezes 20.0%; and the free air volume is 1407 mm3, whose air spring resonates at 840 Hz, far below the 3600 Hz drive point. ce-cad check() also PASSES: ten valid closed solids, 45 interference pairs clear, both declared keep-out zones clear, 10/10 stitched to ground. THE STACK BUDGET CLOSES AT EXACTLY 7.980 mm. What is NOT measured: SPL, IP67, the spring rate, and RF.

summary: THE CHECKS CAN FAIL, AND THEY DID. On the iteration before this one, two of them went red and both were real defects, not test noise: (1) 'bayonet mechanism' probe D reported 3.3145 mm3 with the door pressed 0.250 mm and twisted, because the carrier's floor sat at z=2.290 while the pressed tabs reach z=2.440 — the door could not be opened at all; (2) ce-cad's interference check reported a 0.134433 mm3 clash between the door and the cell, because the cell had been seated on a Ø19.60 contact circle when a flat disc in an R92 saucer rests on its Ø20.00 rim. Both were fixed by moving the geometry (floor to z=2.500, seat diameter to 20.00), never by loosening a check. Recorded because a check nobody has seen fail is not a check.
by: claude (halo lane M, mechanical), ce-cad bin/cad design.py, 2026-09-04

summary: A SECOND CHECK WENT RED, AND IT SHIPPED ONCE BEFORE IT DID. The FDM prototype door was built at the shell's 1.200 mm printed wall, and nothing measured the printed variants against anything — check() only ever saw the moulded parts. The exported STL, read back by tools/stl_bbox.py, came out 25.920 x 26.174 x 3.090 mm against the moulded 26.075 x 26.372 x 2.190: a 1.200 mm wall makes the door's bore Ø22.95, which buries it 0.60 mm radially inside the carrier's Ø24.15 seal land, and a 1.200 mm tab reaches z=3.090 against a carrier floor at 2.500. It could not have been assembled. FIXED by giving the door its own FDM_DOOR_WALL = 0.500 mm (one 0.4 mm extrusion at 125 percent line width) and holding the tabs at the stamped 0.300 mm, because the tab's axial budget belongs to the bayonet and not to the printer. A NEW CHECK, check_fdm_variants(), now measures the printed door and the printed shell against the SAME carrier on every build and would have caught it: printed door 0.0000 mm3, printed shell 0.0000 mm3, printed height 2.190 against the moulded 2.190. Recorded because the defect was invisible to every check that existed, and the file that caught it was a 40-line stdlib STL reader.

SUPERSEDES this folder's earlier row naming the same artifact. out/mech/verdicts.json was rebuilt when two more measured checks were added — 'FDM variants assemble' (the printed door and the printed shell measured against the SAME carrier, after a 1.200 mm printed door wall was found to bury itself 0.60 mm inside the carrier's seal land) and 'shell wall' (thinnest measured section 0.698 mm at (-7.01, -12.62, 2.31), sample step 0.671 mm, against a designed 0.52 mm bore lip). TWELVE measured checks now, all PASS, and the file's sha256 is 987ca5ef544dba5f4a4c6e543d5c465f9a08e15accf74941d3b42f7ea46cc7ec. The earlier row is history and stays: it is what the artifact was when that measurement was taken (TRIAD.md, 'Correcting an artifact — supersede, never edit a row').
